that nobody tells you

slides.text:
Rule no. 1
The blanket belongs to whoever pulls harder.
slides.visual: Premium top-down bed view. One blanket is pulled from both sides in a cute tug-of-war. Both partners are under the blanket on top of the mattress; messy hair and feet peek out from opposite sides. Hands and wrists clearly emerge from natural shoulder/side positions above the mattress, gripping the blanket corners. No hand, arm, or body part comes from under the bed, floor, or bed frame. One pillow has fallen to the floor. The tug-of-war feels cute and ridiculous, not aggressive.

slides.text:
Rule no. 3
There is no such thing as “my snack” after marriage.
slides.visual: Night kitchen. The fridge is open and casts a soft dramatic glow. Aachu is caught holding Zuv's hidden chocolate or chips, cheeks slightly guilty but mischievous. Zuv stands silently behind her like a calm detective, one eyebrow raised, not angry. The fridge shelves, wrapper, and hand position clearly prove snack theft. Warm comedy, not shame. Generate the exact slide text in the clean upper-middle paper area as part of the illustration; do not leave it blank for later.

Rule no. 4
If one person says “nothing,” the case is definitely not closed.

Zuv sits beside her, confused and gentle, holding a water bottle or phone like he is trying to decode what happened. The distance is small enough to feel safe. Soft funny tension.

slides.text:
Rule no. 5
One person will remember the fight.
The other will remember what was ordered for dinner.
slides.visual: Premium warm evening dining-table scene after a tiny couple fight. Aachu leans forward mid-rant, expressive hand raised, animated but lovable, not cruel. Zuv sits close enough to show he is listening, but his eyes keep drifting with helpless tenderness toward a steaming plate of momos and a plain food delivery bag because dinner is getting cold. One of his hands rests near the food, the other stays turned toward her, showing he is trying to balance love and dinner. Soft lamp light, real home table, ceramic plates, no brand labels. Observational intimacy: funny, specific, affectionate, and visually richer than a flat table gag.

slides.text:
Rule no. 7
Marriage is mostly asking,
“Phone kahan hai?”
while holding the phone.
slides.visual: Rebuilt premium living-room setup, not cluttered. Aachu kneels beside a sofa in the lower half of the frame, lifting one cushion with one hand while the missing phone is plainly visible in her other hand, screen dark with no readable UI. Zuv leans from the sofa edge with a patient amused smile, gently pointing at the phone in her hand, trying not to laugh. The room feels lived-in but clean: soft throw blanket, one cup, a small side table, muted plants, warm off-white wall. Clear staged action, clear hand-phone proof, no chaotic pileup, no ugly visual mess.

slides.text:
Rule no. 8
There are no real rules.
Bas ek dusre ki aadat ban jao.
slides.visual: Romantic quiet ending after the chaos. Aachu and Zuv sit on the floor by a sofa near a softly lit window, wrapped in one shared blanket. Aachu leans her head on Zuv's shoulder; Zuv tilts gently toward her, one hand resting over hers near a small shared snack bowl. The room is calm now, with only a few softened traces of the earlier rulebook chaos in the background. Warm neutral ivory light, intimate body closeness, tiny smile, soft belonging. This should feel like observational intimacy and home, not a messy aftermath gag.
